Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner incorrectly applied a simplified version of scientific falsification (Popperian) to a multiple-choice question. In actual scientific practice, when new evidence emerges, the standard procedure is to verify the new evidence and re-evaluate the old hypothesis against it, rather than immediately discarding the old hypothesis (Option A) or rejecting the new one (Option B). The most scientifically accurate and "likely" result described in standard testing contexts for this scenario is that the evidence will be verified before any revisions to the old hypothesis are made (Option D). The Planner jumped to a conclusion of immediate replacement without acknowledging the necessary step of verification and peer review, leading to the wrong answer (A) instead of the correct answer (D).
